question: Question linked to image nº11 Which treatment is most appropriate in the previous patient?

options.opa: Cytoreductive surgery followed by chemotherapy type Rituximab-CHOP until complete remission.
options.opb: Rituximab-CHOP / 21 x 6-8 cycles followed by retroperitoneal radiotherapy.
options.opc: Rituximab-CHOP / 21 x 6-8 cycles followed by intensive QT and stem-cell transplantation (TASPE).
options.opd: Intensive chemotherapy that includes Rituximab, high doses of cyclophosphamide and CNS prophylaxis.
options.ope: Delay treatment until PET-CT and then treat with Rituximab-CHOP / 14 x 6-8 cycles.

analysis: The most appropriate treatment for the patient would be Rituximab-CHOP followed by intensive QT and stem-cell transplantation (TASPE) due to the presence of high-grade lymphoma with bulky disease. This approach aims to achieve complete remission and potentially cure the patient.
